🇺🇸 ULA's Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon satellites

A Vulcan rocket from United Launch Alliance (ULA), the Boeing and Lockheed Martin joint venture, failed on Sunday after lifting off from Cape Canaveral, Florida. All 40 satellites it was carrying for Amazon's Leo internet network were lost.

ULA says the rocket "suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit." It hasn't said what went wrong. This is the company's first total mission failure since it was founded in 2006.

It was Vulcan's first flight in nine months. The rocket had been grounded after problems with its solid rocket boosters. It was also the first of 38 Vulcan launches Amazon has bought to build out Leo, its answer to Elon Musk's Starlink. Before Sunday, Amazon had only about 398 satellites in orbit. It needs 3,236 for global coverage.

The failure is expected to ground Vulcan again for an indefinite period. Vulcan is also contracted to fly roughly half of the US military's national security launches, so the Pentagon will now lean even harder on SpaceX.

🎙 ECO members back Iran’s proposal to end war: Foreign Minister Araghchi

📌 Islamabad, IRNA — Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says that member states of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) have welcomed Tehran’s proposed two-day initiative and expressed hope that it would bring a complete and lasting end to the ongoing war in the region.

Speaking to reporters after the 30th meeting of ECO foreign ministers in Islamabad on Monday, Araghchi said all items on the meeting’s agenda had been discussed.
​
Araghchi said ECO members had responded positively to Iran’s two-day proposal, voicing support and hope that it would lead to a permanent and complete end to the ongoing war.
​
He described member states’ backing for the initiative as one of the notable outcomes of Monday’s meeting.
​
Araghchi said the ministers had also exchanged views on the future and reviewed cooperation in energy, renewable energy, science and regional security.
​
He also emphasized the delegates’ attention to Gaza and the suffering of Palestinians, which has its roots in crimes committed by the Israeli regime.
​
A silent genocide is taking place, Araghchi said, adding that the Israeli regime was preventing Palestinians from accessing medicine, safe drinking water, and food. Severe flooding and heavy rainfall had further aggravated the situation, he said.
​
Participants called for international aid to be delivered to Gaza and for conditions there to change, the foreign minister added.
